chapter_name: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the dramatic era of the 1960s and 70s: Prime Ministerial successions, the great split in the Congress party, and Indira Gandhi's spectacular political comeback!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: After Jawaharlal Nehru's death in 1964, there was fear about whether democracy would survive. Lal Bahadur Shastri peacefully took over, followed by Indira Gandhi in 1966, proving the maturity of Indian democracy.
For the first time, Congress lost its massive majority in the Lok Sabha and lost power in multiple state assemblies. This era introduced coalition politics and 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' (defections).

A power struggle erupted between Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and the 'Syndicate' (a group of powerful, conservative older Congress leaders). This led to a formal split into Congress (O) led by the Syndicate, and Congress (R) led by Indira.

Facing a 'Grand Alliance' of opposition parties in 1971, Indira Gandhi bypassed traditional party structures by directly appealing to the poor with the powerful, populist slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty).

Indira Gandhi won a massive mandate in 1971, and combined with the victory in the 1971 war, she completely restored Congress dominance. However, it was a new kind of Congress dependent entirely on her supreme leadership.

fun_activity.title: 📣 Slogan Maker
fun_activity.instructions: 'Garibi Hatao' changed the course of Indian politics because it was simple and targeted a massive problem. Create a catchy 2-3 word slogan in English or Hindi that addresses a major problem students face today!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define the 'Syndicate'—it refers to the powerful and influential leaders from within the Congress who controlled the party organization.
📌 Explain the phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' in the context of the frequent party defections by MLAs in 1967.
📌 Note that the 'Restoration' of Congress was actually a reinvention; the party was no longer an umbrella coalition but heavily centralized around Indira Gandhi.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 1960s were considered a 'dangerous decade' due to unresolved problems like poverty, inequality, and two successions.
⭐ The 1969 Presidential election was the flashpoint for the Congress split, where V.V. Giri (Indira's candidate) defeated N. Sanjeeva Reddy (Syndicate's candidate).
⭐ Indira Gandhi's radical socialist policies included the abolition of the Privy Purse (allowances given to former princes).
